overview: Chaturmas is a significant four-month period in the Jain religious calendar, observed during the rainy season, typically from July to November. During Chaturmas, Jain monks and nuns stay in one place to avoid harming the multitude of new life forms that emerge during the monsoon. This period is marked by increased religious activities, including fasting, meditation, and scriptural study, both for monks and the lay community. Lay Jains often engage in spiritual practices, attend sermons, and participate in community service. The period is also a time for reflection, purification, and spiritual growth, with many devotees taking additional vows or observing specific austerities.

primary_sources.title: Kalpa Sutra
primary_sources.author: Bhadrabahu
primary_sources.translation: During Chaturmas, monks shall remain in one place for their vows.
primary_sources.notes: The Kalpa Sutra is a key Jain text that outlines monastic conduct and rituals.

misconceptions.myth: Chaturmas is only for monks and nuns.
misconceptions.reality: While monks and nuns strictly observe Chaturmas, laypeople also participate in increased religious activities and practices.
